sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Makomako or wineberry is a fast-growing, often dioecious small tree endemic to New Zealand. It can reach about 10 m in moist forest margins and river valleys. Its leaves are toothed and may show pink beneath; small fleshy berries are about 5 × 4 mm and ripen from red to dark purple-black.

sections.title: Fruit and image
sections.text: The juicy berries are edible and were eaten by Māori; the seeds are bitter. Birds also eat the fruit. The plate's foliage and clustered red-black berries match the species.
